source_snapshot.criteria: System does not boot; BMC and recovered UEFI SEL record unsupported CPU configuration; lightpath identifies failing CPU(s); system fault light is on.

historical_reviews.deepseek: The physical step cannot be automated, but an all-NO classification loses meaningful OOB observation and post-recovery validation.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly separates manual hardware custody from automatable evidence collection.

historical_reviews.v3_1: Requires exactly one approved mismatch dimension where feasible, because changing link speed, cores, power and frequency together prevents attribution and may produce a different platform policy outcome.

original_test_intent: Verify that the platform rejects a controlled mismatched-CPU pair, records the correct configuration fault in BMC and UEFI evidence, identifies the affected socket(s), asserts the system fault indicator, and recovers with the supported pair.
original_method: A qualified technician installs an approved pair differing in a declared compatibility dimension; automation records exact CPUID/part/socket identity, observes the bounded boot rejection and OOB faults, then validates recovered UEFI SEL and system health after the supported pair is restored.
manual_activity: Qualified technician performs powered-down CPU installation/restoration under ESD, torque and thermal controls and confirms physical lightpath/fault indicators that lack reliable telemetry.
required_inputs: Two CPU part numbers, steppings and CPUID data
Declared mismatch dimension and platform rule
Expected BMC/UEFI event IDs and socket mapping
safety_requirements: Agent never performs physical CPU work
Qualified technician uses power discharge, ESD, torque and thermal-interface controls
Verify both CPUs are individually electrically/mechanically safe
Maintain independent BMC and recovery access
Stop on abnormal heat/current or wrong fault
Verify cooling, inventory and health after recovery
agent_execution_scope: Capture baseline matched-pair inventory and health
Verify approved parts, sockets and mismatch matrix
Collect BMC event and indicator telemetry
Verify matched inventory, thermals and health
engineer_actions: Approve the exact mismatched and recovery pairs
Define boot timeout and expected fault signature

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The narrative correctly refuses agent-performed CPU replacement but gives no bounded OOB commands, exact pair, mismatch dimension, timeout or recovery evidence plan.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Automate read-only BMC inventory, power/POST timeline, event capture and post-restoration health around a qualified technician's controlled pair swap; do not automate physical work or repeated power cycling.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Two mismatched same-type CPUs, the listed mismatch dimensions, boot attempt, BMC/UEFI evidence, indicators and 20/10-minute timing are preserved; exact parts and sockets are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a mismatch matrix that freezes all attributes except the intended dimension, plus socket-tagged photos, OOB event timeline, boot deadline and signed recovery report.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the causal mismatch and negative boot result measurable while separating manual custody from automation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Distinguishes a platform compatibility rejection from installation error, individual unsupported CPU, power fault or unrelated POST hang.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some commercial CPU pairs differ in several fused attributes; if isolation is impossible, the test can show pair rejection but cannot attribute it to one dimension.

project_override_considerations: This is a pair-mismatch case, distinct from row 1423's individually unsupported CPUs. Each CPU should be supported alone where the platform allows; otherwise the evidence cannot isolate mismatch behavior.
expected_evidence: BMC inventory and exact fault events
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criteria consistently target rejection of a mismatched pair. Multiple example mismatch dimensions broaden selection but do not conflict once the project chooses the controlled pair.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The pair, mismatch dimension, lab controls and recovery configuration are finite project inputs. Absence after the normal request would block execution, not static review.

review_improvement: Preserves operator-only hardware work, recovers automation value, and prevents a random no-boot or individually unsupported processor from being accepted as evidence of pair mismatch detection.
independent_technical_reasoning: A mismatch test requires both processors to be individually admissible enough that the pair relationship, not a single unsupported part, causes rejection. Exact socket identity, a bounded boot-stage oracle and expected event mapping establish that causality. Physical replacement remains manual, while OOB evidence and recovery health are automatable, so REQUIRES is the correct classification.
